answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable sequence of dependent modular squarings before it can participate. Because each result feeds the next, GPUs cannot parallelize one identity’s computation to reduce its elapsed time; creating many clones requires many independent sequences and still leaves a physical time bottleneck for each. Like paths through a karst orchard ending at a reef, the proofs can be checked efficiently, while producing them cannot be shortcut by parallel hardware.
